members.note: An eased scroll here glides over a fixed DURATION rather than interpolating at a fixed speed, so the knob is a duration. Same feel, different parameterisation; UDreamLayoutContainerScrollBox carries the speed-based form under UMG's name for the layout road.
Pushed to UUIScrollView::bEnableTouchScrolling; the gate is the event system's current input device, because a finger and a mouse both arrive as pointer 0.
One stored bit: UUIScrollView::AllowEventBubbleUp, asked the other way round. Get/SetConsumePointerInput on the behaviour is the inverse view of it.

Invalid by default = whatever the input preset routes here (the right stick), which is today's behaviour. A named key narrows it; the preset only binds the right stick's two axes, so any other key needs a project binding.
Already on the base of every widget; a second one on this control would shadow it (UHT error) and be a second answer.
FDreamScrollBoxStyle, resolved against the project style sheet. Get/SetStyle.
The box's style carries the bar's whole style, so one edit dresses the box and its bar together.
Same name and meaning; the type is EDreamPanelOrientation rather than TEnumAsByte<EOrientation>, which is this library's own two-value spelling.
EDreamScrollBoxScrollbarVisibility (Permanent / AutoHide) plus bShowScrollBar for 'no bar at all', instead of UMG's ESlateVisibility. This library has no Slate visibility enum.
EDreamScrollBoxConsumeMouseWheel, the same three answers; pushed to UUIScrollView.

A reader/writer pair on the control (Get/SetScrollbarThickness), not a second field: the style is the one truth. A float, because a bar has one thickness across its own axis; UMG's FVector2D spells a second number nothing here uses.
New style field, default FMargin(0) = what every bar has drawn. Counted into the gutter, because the gutter is everything the viewport gives up for the bar.
Permanent IS always-show, so IsAlwaysShowScrollbar / SetAlwaysShowScrollbar read and write that enum rather than a flag beside it.
Keeps the bar node and its gutter while sleeping the handle. Default false = today's behaviour.
Pushed to UUIScrollView::bAllowOverscroll, which gates the out-of-range damper rather than zeroing the author's number.
A whole window of leading space, as Slate spends (not the half window the plan sketched). Writable at runtime here; UMG's is construction-only.
A whole window of trailing space. Writable at runtime, unlike UMG's.
EDreamUIScrollDestination, now with BottomOrRight so all four of UMG's answers exist.
Writable at runtime here; UMG's is construction-only.
Default AnimatedScroll, not UMG's NoScroll: navigation here has always revealed its target, and NoScroll would stop every existing gamepad-driven list from following focus.

Asked once at drag-begin, so a gesture that was refused stays refused for its whole length. The drag scrolls from the press, the move that crossed the drag threshold included, as SScrollBox's does, so the content stays under the pointer that grabbed it. A right drag that starts on the box's own bar scrolls nothing: the bar answers the left button only (UDreamScrollBar::AcceptedMouseButtons, SScrollBar's rule) and the view that drags the content sits on the viewport beside the bar, so the gesture reaches neither -- where SScrollBox, which the unanswered press bubbles up to, would drag the content with it.
Scales ScrollSensitivity, which is the DISTANCE one notch covers. Same name and meaning as the list controls'.
Takes a float; writes the style and switches StyleSource to Inline, so the next style push does not throw the number away.
See the property row: this library's eased scroll is duration-based.
Drops the fling and leaves any open rubber band to spring shut, which is not inertia.
On the base, with the property.
On the base, with the property.

An offset, as UMG reports. Fires only for changes the player made: everything this control pushes itself is flagged at the moment of the push, which is the only place the two roads are distinguishable.
A bool rather than an ESlateVisibility, which this library has none of. Fired from the style push, and only on a change.

The event is the one every widget already has, UDreamWidget::OnFocusReceived (UserIndex, PointerId); what the box adds is the relay, since the event system focuses the FACE and not the control. A UUISelectable added to the FACE on demand and gated on the base's bIsFocusable, which is off by default -- so no existing box becomes a navigation candidate. The selectable is what the event system hands focus to and what already tells a resting pointer from focus, so its state IS received and lost; only the EDGE is announced, because that state is re-applied for repaints too.
UDreamWidget::OnFocusLost, relayed from the face: the other edge of the same subscription, under the same gate.

Focus moving INSIDE the box, carrying the widget that took it. Not gated on bIsFocusable -- the content is focusable whether or not the box is. Raised by the navigation reveal through UUIScrollView::NotifyContentFocusMoved: that walk is the one place that knows both which widget took focus and which scrolling ancestors contain it, and polling HasFocusedDescendants would be a tick for an edge.
Signed: negative before the start, positive past the end, zero in range and zero while overscroll is off.
Per cent of the window, as SScrollBox reports.
The progress the behaviour already maintains; not a second division.

All four parameters, with the destination and padding appended so the old two-argument call keeps its meaning: Configured and a negative padding both mean 'whatever this box is set up with'. The same signature on UUIScrollView and UDreamLayoutContainerScrollBox.
